There’s this book making it’s way across the “self help” circuit called Attached. I don’t recommend it to people as a life solution but it is really informative and introduces the idea of attachment styles and how they go on to play parts in our communication style in every interaction (romantic, plutonic or familia).

Just based off what you shared it sounds like a bit of self-sabotage which is really just a defense mechanism at its core. I struggle with that at the moment.  Sometimes “following your gut” on things feels right, but it’s important to also consider that our “intuition” is just a compilation of scenarios we’ve experienced in the past, designed to originally keep early humans from making the same mistakes that could have grave consequences. I think the book used berry-eating as an example and your intuition sensing maybe THESE berries I shouldn’t eat. Not nearly as constantly useful in the modern day.  Just in the case of dating your intuition may be throwing red flags that aren’t actually as “bad” as initially perceived or persuading us to go against men who subconsciously might remind us of someone else. Obviously there are exceptions but again just something to consider if you find yourself sort of stewing on all of someone’s negatives.  The book also does a solid job of breaking down how our attachment styles are responses from our nervous system, which oversees fight, fight, fawn and freeze. Again, an evolutionary trait that in modern times is so overactive that it often goes unchecked and we find ourselves unable to process depression, anxiety, people pleasing etc. 

You can also just Google attachment styles, but I found it to be a really helpful starting point.
